meta.note: Every value here is binding. A render that deviates from any of it is a bug, not a variation. Change the version before changing a value, and never change an entry under `invariants` without a measured reason.

safe_areas.note: The Shorts player draws its own UI over the frame. Nothing that carries meaning may enter these bands.

block_phases.name: enter
block_phases.note: cards fly in, A then B, 80ms stagger

block_phases.name: reveal
block_phases.note: bars fill and numbers count up together

block_phases.name: hold
block_phases.note: result stays on screen; VO lands its line here

block_phases.name: exit
block_phases.note: both cards leave toward opposite edges

timeline.rationale: 41-60s is the only duration band that performs in this niche (median 26,239 views vs 751 for 16-25s). 5 blocks x 8.5s + 3.5s end card = 46s sits in the middle of it.

divider.note: VS badge with the timer ring around it

color.note: Two option colors, one urgency color, nothing else. A third option color would break recognizability at thumbnail size, which is where this palette does its work.

motion.note: Motion is functional here: it separates the two options in space and marks the reveal in time. Decoration competes with the decision.

voiceover.tone: fast, dry, mildly provocative; never explains the joke

music.note: One track per 20-episode arc. Viewers ask for the song name in the comments; a stable track turns that into a recurring comment we can answer.

copy_rules.framing_note: Drawn from the audience's own vocabulary in 1,001 mined comments: never (103), unlimited (38), always (33). Words the audience already uses need no decoding time.
copy_rules.ramp_note: Block 1 is the hook and must land in under 2 seconds of reading. Block 5 is the one people argue about in the comments.

reveal_mechanic.fabrication_note: The top comment across every breakout video mined is people mocking percentages that do not add up ('How tf is 90 % and 15%', 148 likes). Invented survey numbers are both dishonest and, demonstrably, noticed. Percentages come from a real Community-tab poll on the previous episode, or the block states a prediction with no number at all.
reveal_mechanic.split_note: Under 55/45 reads as a coin flip and provokes nothing. Over 88/12 reads as a non-dilemma. The comment engine is the viewer discovering they are in a minority they did not expect to be in.

end_card.cta_rule: One line, one ask, pointing at the poll. Never 'like and subscribe'.
end_card.loop_note: Last frame matches the first frame's background exactly so the Shorts loop is seamless.

invariants: Option A is always on top and always #FF2D6F; option B is always below and always #00D1FF
The timer is always the yellow ring at the centre, between the two cards, and always runs exactly 3500ms
Anton for options, Inter 900 for numbers
Percentages always sum to 100 and are never invented
No intro: frame 1 is already a dilemma
No borrowed IP, characters, or footage
